title: "AWS Water Positive Public Launch" internal memo
what_it_shows: Memo written about a month before the Nov 2022 launch projected AWS primary water use of about 7.7bn gallons/yr by 2030. It advised counting only primary (on-site) water and keeping secondary (power-generation) and company-wide figures confidential, noting that indirect use is about 90% of Amazon's water footprint.
public_claim_contradicted: AWS 'water positive by 2030' pledge to return more water than it uses, made without disclosing data-center water consumption.
company_response: Disputed: Amazon called the memo 'obsolete' and its models 'preliminary and unvetted'; said water use per kWh is down 40% since 2021.

title: Wangusi v. Amazon Web Services and Virginia Connects (Arlington Co. Cir. Ct. CL26002535-00)
company: Amazon Web Services; Virginia Connects (Data Center Coalition network)
what_it_shows: Former AWS water sustainability program manager alleges FOIA'd utility billing records show Northern Virginia year-over-year drops of 0.8% and 32.1%, not the 42% AWS advertised, and year-round withdrawals. He also alleges local replenishment covers about 22-25% of use and that Virginia Connects ran a coordinated ad campaign on the same day.
public_claim_contradicted: AWS claims of a 42% Northern Virginia water cut, '75% of the way to water positive', and outside-air cooling ~97% of the year.
company_response: Disputed: AWS denies wrongdoing/declined comment; says 2025 water data was third-party assured.

title: SourceMaterial/Guardian investigation of permit filings in water-scarce regions (incl. Aragon permit applications)
what_it_shows: Mapping of 632 sites from permits and filings found 38 active and 24 planned Amazon/Microsoft/Google data centers in water-scarce regions; Amazon sought a 48% water increase at three Aragon sites. Former AWS water manager Nathan Wangusi said he raised internally that the offsetting approach was 'not ethical'.
public_claim_contradicted: Water-positive/replenishment pledges and claims that siting accounts for local water scarcity.
company_response: Amazon and Google said they consider water scarcity in siting; Microsoft declined to comment.

title: The Dalles, Oregon: Google water-use records released after public-records lawsuit
what_it_shows: The city sued The Oregonian to keep Google's water use secret as a trade secret; the settlement released 2012-2021 data showing Google used 355m gallons in 2021, about 29% of city water, roughly triple 2017.
public_claim_contradicted: Google's portrayal of water stewardship while treating site-level water use as a trade secret.
company_response: Google later said it would no longer treat site-level US water figures as trade secrets.

title: Racine records on Microsoft Mount Pleasant data center water use
what_it_shows: After a ~210-day delay while the city reviewed with Microsoft (which had asked for trade-secret treatment), and a lawsuit by Midwest Environmental Advocates, records showed peak use up to 702,000 gal/day and about 8.4m gal/yr at buildout.
public_claim_contradicted: Microsoft messaging that new closed-loop designs avoid ongoing municipal water use for cooling.
company_response: Microsoft waived the trade-secret request; says use is 'significantly lower' than many industrial customers.

title: Botetourt County FOIA emails: Google and Western Virginia Water Authority
what_it_shows: FOIA'd emails show Google discussing demands of 10-11 million gallons/day with the water authority, while residents had been told maximum use would be 2 million gal/day.
public_claim_contradicted: Public assurances that the Botetourt data center would use at most 2 MGD.
company_response: Water authority says larger figures were early requests it mostly rejected; no Google comment reported.

title: Pima County-AWS nondisclosure agreement for 'Project Blue'
company: Amazon Web Services; Beale Infrastructure; Pima County
what_it_shows: NDA obtained via public records names AWS as the end user and commits the county to secrecy for five years, with advance notice so AWS can seek a protective order against records requests.
public_claim_contradicted: Developer's statement that no company was behind Project Blue other than Beale Infrastructure.
company_response: AWS said it did standard due diligence; Beale denied agreements with AWS.

title: SELC aerial imagery and permit record: xAI Colossus gas turbines, Memphis
what_it_shows: Aerial photos showed 35 methane turbines (~422 MW) at the site, versus permit applications for 15, operating without an air permit; SELC says xAI is likely Memphis's largest industrial NOx source.
public_claim_contradicted: xAI/booster claims that operations were permitted, minor-polluting and fully compliant.
company_response: No xAI response reported; Shelby County Health Dept. disagrees with SELC's Clean Air Act view.

title: 'Facts Over Fear' and Greater Memphis Chamber mailers for xAI
company: xAI; Greater Memphis Chamber; anonymous 'Facts Over Fear'
what_it_shows: Anonymous mailers said only 15 turbines ran and emissions resembled a gas station; a Chamber mailer listed nine 'oversight' agencies, two of which (MLGW, TDEC) said they had no such authority. The Chamber managed xAI's PR.
public_claim_contradicted: Claims that xAI is a minor polluter in full compliance with all regulations.
company_response: Chamber's Bobby White said he used 'regulatory' loosely; xAI did not respond.

title: Microsoft employee memos, call transcripts and SEC whistleblower filing on AI for oil & gas
what_it_shows: A late-2021 employee memo calculated one Exxon deal could enable emissions equal to 640% of Microsoft's 2021 carbon-removal target; documents were later submitted to the SEC in a whistleblower complaint alleging omitted climate harms.
public_claim_contradicted: Microsoft's public pitch of AI as a climate solution and its carbon-negative-by-2030 pledge.
company_response: Microsoft said tech can help industry decarbonize and cited its 2030 goals.

title: Microsoft 2024 Environmental Sustainability Report (FY2023)
what_it_shows: Emissions rose 29-40% above the 2020 baseline, driven by Scope 3 from data center construction; water use up 87% since 2020 to ~2.1bn gallons.
public_claim_contradicted: Carbon-negative and water-positive by 2030 pledges.
company_response: Microsoft says it remains committed and on track.

title: Google 2024 Environmental Report; end of carbon-neutral claim
what_it_shows: Emissions reached 14.3 MtCO2e in 2023, up 48% vs 2019, driven by data-center energy; Google warned AI may make cuts 'challenging' and quietly stopped claiming operational carbon neutrality (claimed since 2007 via offsets).
public_claim_contradicted: Long-running 'carbon neutral' branding and 24/7 carbon-free/net-zero 2030 messaging.
company_response: Google acknowledged it stopped maintaining operational carbon neutrality in 2023.

title: Entergy Louisiana application for three gas plants for Meta Hyperion (LPSC Docket U-32146)
what_it_shows: Filing seeks >$3.7bn for ~2,300 MW of gas plants under a 15-year Meta contract; cost figures and Meta's load increase were redacted or 'attorney's eyes only', and intervenor testimony estimated potential customer costs of hundreds of millions to billions.
public_claim_contradicted: Claims that Meta will pay its way and ratepayers are insulated from data-center costs.
company_response: Entergy's filings assert ratepayers are mostly insulated; no direct response in source.

title: PJM Independent Market Monitor report on capacity costs; Google exec remark
what_it_shows: Monitoring Analytics found data centers added ~$9.3-9.4bn to PJM capacity costs; a Google energy executive told PJM's annual meeting Google is 'imposing a significant cost on the system'.
public_claim_contradicted: Industry ads saying data centers pay their own costs so families don't.
company_response: PJM said report affirms supply/demand drove prices; Google's exec acknowledged costs.

title: AEP Ohio PUCO filings after data center tariff
what_it_shows: Once the tariff required financial commitments, the data center pipeline fell from 30+ GW to ~13 GW studied and ~5.6 GW signed; AEP conceded many earlier requests were speculative or duplicative.
public_claim_contradicted: Utility/industry load-growth projections used to justify grid build-out and rate increases.
company_response: AEP says tariff is working; Ohio Manufacturers' Association calls forecasts inflated.

title: FERC filings on Talen Susquehanna-Amazon co-located nuclear data center
what_it_shows: AEP and Exelon told FERC the amended deal could shift up to $140m/yr in transmission costs to PJM ratepayers; FERC rejected the amended agreement 2-1.
public_claim_contradicted: Claims that behind-the-meter nuclear deals are clean and cost-free to other customers.
company_response: Talen called the cost-shift estimate baseless and said FERC erred.

title: Georgia Dept. of Audits data center tax exemption review (revised)
what_it_shows: State audit found $474m forgone in FY2025 and only ~30% of data centers attributable to the exemption; a correction cut job estimates to less than a third (operations jobs 5,471 to 1,641).
public_claim_contradicted: Industry claims of large job creation and that tax breaks pay for themselves.
company_response: No industry response reported.

title: Texas Comptroller testimony/audits of data center sales tax exemption
company: Texas data center industry; Data Center Coalition
what_it_shows: Comptroller said the $3.2bn two-year cost estimate is almost certainly too low; of 20 audited data centers, six were out of compliance, at least four on job requirements.
public_claim_contradicted: Industry/PwC claims of 103,000 jobs and broad economic benefits.
company_response: Data Center Coalition warned repeal would end Texas's rise as a data center market.

title: Meta Hyperion tax abatement via Delaware affiliate Laidley LLC
what_it_shows: Richland Parish approved a 20-year sales tax exemption for Laidley LLC, a Meta affiliate, estimated at ~$3.3bn+ in forgone revenue, against a pledge of ~500 permanent jobs.
public_claim_contradicted: Meta's messaging on local economic and tax benefits of Hyperion.
company_response: Meta did not comment.

title: Oracle 'Project Jupiter Together' lobbying disclosure to NM State Ethics Commission
what_it_shows: Under Ethics Commission pressure Oracle disclosed $3.44m paid to Brabender Cox for ads, polling, canvassing and paid influencers aimed at the air permit for the site's gas microgrid.
public_claim_contradicted: Ads presenting broad grassroots support and economic benefits (7,000 construction jobs claim).
company_response: Oracle said disclosure was voluntary and for transparency.

title: NM Ethics Commission v. Elevate New Mexico (complaint and settlement)
company: Yucca Growth Infrastructure LLC (Project Jupiter power applicant)
what_it_shows: Lawsuit forced the anonymous ad group to disclose $3.67m, all from Yucca Growth Infrastructure, the gas-plant permit applicant, used to urge NMED to approve air permits.
public_claim_contradicted: Ads presented as independent community voices backing the project.
company_response: Elevate denied wrongdoing; disclosed 'in the spirit of good faith'.

title: NMED comment-portal records: form letters under residents' names (Project Jupiter)
what_it_shows: Identical pro-Project Jupiter form letters on the state comment portal carried names of residents who said they told canvassers they were skeptical or opposed.
public_claim_contradicted: Claims of strong public support in permit comments.
company_response: Oracle acknowledged canvassers but denied authorizing comments without consent.

title: Oregon Connects registration (Data Center Coalition state ad network)
company: Data Center Coalition (Microsoft, Google, Meta, QTS, Equinix members)
what_it_shows: Business filings show DCC's president registered 'Oregon Connects' as a social-welfare group; the network (Virginia, Pennsylvania, NC, Texas, Ohio, Indiana Connects) runs TV ads without disclosing funders.
public_claim_contradicted: Ad claim that data centers are 'committed to paying their costs, so Oregon families don't'.
company_response: DCC said the campaign seeks to better explain data centers; declined to name funders.

title: EU FOI records: Microsoft/DigitalEurope lobbying for confidential data-centre reporting
company: Microsoft; DigitalEurope (Amazon, Google, Meta, Apple members)
what_it_shows: Records show Microsoft and DigitalEurope asked the Commission to make individual data-centre metrics confidential; the final delegated act copied the language almost word-for-word, hiding site-level energy, water and renewables data.
public_claim_contradicted: Microsoft's public statement that it supports greater transparency around data centres.
company_response: Microsoft reiterated transparency support, did not answer lobbying questions; others no comment.

title: Leaked NRSC memo to AI companies on data center backlash
company: National Republican Senatorial Committee; AI companies
what_it_shows: Private memo told AI firms data centers are a 'sleeper issue' and that internal polling shows them about as popular as spent nuclear waste; urged campaigns explaining who benefits and who pays.
public_claim_contradicted: Industry ads portraying data centers as popular community assets.
company_response: No company response reported.

title: OpenAI threat report on China-linked anti-data-center content vs. 'China funds opposition' claims
what_it_shows: OpenAI's own investigation found a likely China-linked ChatGPT-assisted campaign but no evidence it swayed opinion at scale; NPR found little evidence for claims that China funds US opposition.
public_claim_contradicted: Industry/official claims that local opposition is Chinese-funded or foreign dark money.
company_response: Named Utah groups denied Chinese ties.
